paragraphs.source_en: “For after eating, they invariably take a bath; and after bathing, by some method or other, they vomit up everything they swallowed before the bath, thereby clearing out the stomach. Once this cleansing of the stomach has been accomplished, they sit down again at the banquet table and gorge themselves to their hearts’ content on delicacies from mountain and sea. When they have filled their bellies, they bathe once more and vomit it up again. In this way they may indulge in whatever dainties they desire without the least injury to the organs within. In my humble opinion, such an excellent device may truly be called killing two birds with one stone…”

paragraphs.source_en: “In this twentieth century, when traffic grows ever more frequent and banquets ever more numerous, and moreover in this second year of the war with Russia, when the affairs of the military nation are so pressing, I firmly believe that the time has come for us, citizens of a victorious nation, to imitate the Romans and study this art of bathing and vomiting. Otherwise, I secretly fear that before long all the citizens of our great nation will, like you, become sufferers from stomach disease.”

paragraphs.source_en: “At such a time, I venture to think that if we men well versed in Western affairs were to investigate ancient histories and legends, seek out this long-abandoned secret method, and apply it to Meiji society, we should gain the merit of preventing calamity before it arises, and repay in some small measure the favors that have allowed us our customary pleasures.”

paragraphs.source_en: “For this reason, I have recently been ranging through the works of Gibbon, Mommsen, Smith, and others, but to my deepest regret I have not yet found the slightest clue. However, as you know, I am by nature one who, once I have set my mind upon a matter, never abandons it halfway unless I succeed; I am therefore confident that before long I shall rediscover the method of vomiting. Once I have discovered it, I shall immediately inform you, so pray be at ease and wait patiently. Accordingly, as for the aforementioned treat of tochimenbo and peacock tongues, I shall have the honor of receiving you only after that secret method has been discovered. That will be convenient not only for me, but also of great benefit to you, my dear sir, who are habitually troubled by a weak stomach. Yours in haste.”
